Mr. E.H. Hammond, Supt., Wapato, Wash. Cashman Agency, D. Dear Sir - I take great pleasure to write you. In regards to my children whom you have in your charge, I would be most grateful if you can let them come for the vacation. They were here last vacation and I have a better proposition for Edna this vacation to work for the same folks. I am working for at present at $10 a week as a helper around the house. They are white folks and are very good & appreciative. We have 100 acres of alfalfa hay to cut 3 times this season which I have been practicing will start to cut about next Monday. Also have 60 acres of barley and will constantly need help all summer. The children's names are Edna & Peter Napoleon respectively. Peter will also be given something to do to keep him in good sort. I have a little niece there also named Nabi Napoleon. Mrs. Dan Secora of the Chehalis Reservation would like to take her on this vacation. They are also very good folks. I would desire you to set them on the train at Tacoma in the morning about 7 A.M. To Wapato. If it would be convenient for us to meet on Saturday afternoon so that would give Edna time to enter upon her duties the following Monday. Please let me know when you could get them away. I am sending you a check for their fares. I will await your answer with much anxiety. Remaining yours Truly, Al Napoleon R.R.O. #1, Wapato, Wash. P.S. Since I have started to work here I have made good, $60 first month, $50 second month, $80 for this 3rd month, and the children can do the same if they wish earnestly do their work. Help is scarce in this locality this season owing to the war. Edna W. See Sadie Napoleon folder regarding transfer of Sadie to Cheinawa. Edna to Yak. fair and return of the children to Cushman By Al Napoleon CASE RECORD. NAME: Peter Napoleon Sex: Male Tribe: Bayallup State: Wash. May 26, 1919 Age: 15 years Height: 5 ft. 1 1/2 ins. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for in any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unutilized. Whether the person signing the blank is a parent, guardian, or next of kin, must be given. The person signing the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. Compliance must be given to all orders and instructions which have been promulgated in connection with the new course of study issued December 1, 1915. The information as to public school facilities called for in the certificate of the Superintendent (third page hereof) must be given, and all superintendents are especially directed to exhaust every means to secure enrollment of Indian children in the State public schools, pursuant to instructions heretofore issued in this regard. If pupil's work is not worthy of a rating of fair, no grade should be recorded. Under "Remarks" mention anything that indicates interest, conduct, and proficiency of the pupil.
